What these numbers mean

  • “Works on” for other mods is a static prediction. CDAL checks patterns stored in mod files against the game’s executable code and checks matching CDAL IDs. These results do not confirm that a mod or an individual feature works in game.
  • Players get new CDAL data with Update CDAL.cmd. "Changed meaning" means the game still has that code but it now does something else, so a mod that used it needs a new CDAL ID; the others can come back in a later data update.

Understanding the results

The columns

Mod
The mod’s name, linked to its Nexus Mods page.
Built on CDAL
Yes when the mod is built on CDAL and its author enrolled it.
CDAL ID coverage
How many of the game addresses the mod uses CDAL can give on this game version; for a mod built on CDAL, how many of its features have every ID they need. A line under the count says how many more have a CDAL ID that is waiting for a CDAL update. For other mods this shows what CDAL could give them, not what they use today. Tap or hover a count for details.
Can use CDAL for
What CDAL can do for the mod: every address, CDAL IDs plus its own site pack for the rest, its own site pack, or the hook manager and crash notes only. For other mods this is what CDAL could give them, not what they use today.
Works on 2.05.01
Whether the mod probably still works on this game version. For a mod built on CDAL: whether CDAL has every ID its features need. For other mods: whether the byte patterns in its files still find the game’s code, or, for a mod without byte patterns, whether the places in the game it uses match CDAL’s data. A prediction from data, not a test in game. Hover a mark for the details.
Mod last updated
When the mod’s newest main file was uploaded to Nexus Mods.
Author
Who made the mod.
Track
Add the mod to My mods, a list kept in this browser.

Works on this version: other mods

Whether the mod’s own byte patterns still find the game’s code on this game version, and whether CDAL has IDs for what they match. These are predictions.

  • Likely works

    Every recorded pattern resolved uniquely and all matching CDAL IDs are available. For a mod without byte patterns: every place in the game it was seen using on this game version has a CDAL ID with an address here; or every place it uses has one, and reading its code showed it searches for its places itself; or reading its code showed it uses no game code.

  • Some parts may be broken

    Some patterns did not resolve uniquely, or some matching CDAL IDs are unavailable.

  • Likely broken

    More than half the patterns did not resolve uniquely, or no matching CDAL IDs are available. This is not a confirmed in-game failure.

  • Unknown

    No complete, usable pattern scan for this build. Available CDAL IDs alone are not enough.

  • Unknown: no byte patterns

    CDAL found no byte patterns in the mod’s files, so there is nothing to check. A mod like that may still use the game’s code, found another way (fixed addresses, patterns it builds while running); its CDAL ID coverage counts the places the mod lab saw it use.

  • Unknown: no CDAL ID match

    No prediction is assigned without matching CDAL IDs.

  • Not updated

    The mod said itself that it doesn’t support this game version, none of the places it looks for are found and it was not seen hooking anything, or it uses fixed addresses for an older game version.

Why it broke

When a game update broke one of these mods, a label after the mark says whether CDAL has what it lost. It compares the scan of its files on this version with saved scans of the same files on older versions.

CDAL could fix
Byte patterns stopped finding the game’s code, or now find a different spot than before, and CDAL has an address on this version for every place they found before. Moved to CDAL, the mod would keep working without an update from its author.
Needs new IDs
Some places its broken patterns found have no CDAL ID yet, or no address on this version yet. They can be requested as CDAL IDs.
Other cause
The lab ran it on the version before, it went wrong on this one, and no byte pattern broke: the cause is something CDAL IDs don’t cover, such as changed game data or behaviour.

What a pattern match means

A byte pattern is a sequence a mod can use to locate game code. CDAL’s scanner searches for patterns extracted from the mod’s files, separately from identifying matching CDAL IDs.

A miss can indicate an outdated lookup, but patterns may also be unused, intended for older versions or used as fallbacks. The mod may search different memory regions or apply extra filters.

A match does not verify gameplay or a specific feature.

Built on CDAL

  • Built on CDAL (enrolled)

    The mod is built on CDAL and its author enrolled it. Its Works on column shows whether CDAL has the IDs its features need.

  • Not built on CDAL

    The mod isn’t built on CDAL: it finds the game’s code its own way. When CDAL can read byte patterns from its files (150 of these 365 mods), its Works on column shows the scan prediction; otherwise it shows Unknown.

Works on this version: mods built on CDAL

Whether CDAL has the IDs each declared feature needs on this game version.

  • Likely works

    All declared feature requirements are available.

  • Some features may be off

    Some feature requirements are unavailable.

  • Likely broken

    A core feature or most features have missing requirements.

CDAL ID coverage

How much of what the mod needs CDAL has, counted from the game addresses found in its code and in the mod lab; for a mod built on CDAL, from its features.

All IDs
Every game address it uses has a CDAL ID with an address on this game version, or every feature has its IDs.
Some IDs
Some do: the count and the bar show how many CDAL can give on this game version, and a line under them how many more are waiting for a CDAL update.
No IDs yet
None of the game addresses it uses has a CDAL ID yet. They can be requested as CDAL IDs.
Places not found
Its byte patterns look for places in the game’s code, but none finds its place in this game version, so which addresses it needs isn’t known.
Uses game code, not seen yet
No game address has been seen in it yet, but reading its code showed that it uses the game’s code. The hover says how.
Uses game data
Reading its code showed that it doesn’t use the game’s code but reads or changes game values in memory. Where those values sit can change in a game update, so whether it still works isn’t known yet.
No game code
Reading its code showed that it uses neither the game’s code nor its data, so CDAL has no address to give it. These mods show only with Show mods without game code. The hover says what it does instead.
Not checked yet
No game address was found in it, and its code hasn’t been read yet, so what CDAL can give it isn’t known.
Not run yet
No game address was found in its files, and the mod lab hasn’t run it yet, so which game addresses it uses isn’t known.

Can use CDAL for

What the mod can use CDAL for, worked out from its coverage. Every mod can use the hook manager and crash notes.

Everything
CDAL has an ID for every game address it uses, so it needs no addresses of its own and keeps working after game updates once CDAL’s data is updated. It also gets the shared hook manager and crash notes.
IDs + own site pack
CDAL IDs for the addresses that have one; the rest go in the mod’s own site pack, which CDAL looks up again after game updates. It also gets the shared hook manager and crash notes.
Own site pack
CDAL has no ID yet for the addresses it uses: they go in the mod’s own site pack, or can be requested as CDAL IDs. It also gets the shared hook manager and crash notes.
Hook manager, crash notes
It uses no game address CDAL could provide, but it can still hook through CDAL’s shared hook manager, so it doesn’t clash with other mods, and get CDAL’s crash and hang notes.
Not known yet
Not known yet: which game addresses it uses hasn’t been seen yet, in its files or in the mod lab, so what CDAL can give it isn’t known. Every mod can still use CDAL’s shared hook manager and its crash and hang notes.

It isn’t built on CDAL: this shows what CDAL could give it, not what it uses today.

What the mod needs is judged from the game addresses found in its code and in the lab; a mod that finds addresses another way may need more. For a mod that uses CDAL, it is the IDs its features need.

Mod update dates

Date colors describe upload age only.

  • Green: up to 7 days
  • Amber: 8–30 days
  • Red: over 30 days

Hover a date for its exact time. An older upload alone does not establish a compatibility problem.

Using this page

Hover a status icon for its recorded pattern or CDAL ID counts. Mod names link to their Nexus pages.

Only status summaries are published here. These scans do not verify gameplay.

Excluded Authors by Request

At their request, everything related to these authors' mods has been removed from CDAL: downloaded files, scan and test results, status page rows and any CDAL ID findings that came from their mods. Their mods are left out of all previous and future CDAL updates, and CDAL IDs that are still needed are found again from the game's own code alone.
